R.E.P.O is the kind of game that starts with “okay, let’s do one quick run” and ends with everyone screaming, laughing, and questioning their teamwork skills. It somehow turns simple objectives into absolute chaos in the best way possible. One moment you’re calmly trying to do your job, and the next you’re running for your life while your friends are making *very* unhelpful decisions.

What really makes R.E.P.O shine is how naturally funny it is. The physics, timing, and unexpected disasters feel perfectly designed to create comedy without trying too hard. You don’t even need to be good at the game to have fun—in fact, being bad might make it even better. Every failed attempt feels like a story worth retelling.

The atmosphere is tense enough to keep you on edge, but never so serious that it stops being fun. It balances suspense and humor perfectly, turning panic into laughter almost instantly. And when you play with friends, the game becomes a nonstop highlight reel of mistakes, heroic sacrifices, and blaming each other for everything that goes wrong.

Overall, R.E.P.O is pure fun. It’s goofy, stressful, unpredictable, and endlessly entertaining. If you enjoy games that create unforgettable moments, inside jokes, and lots of laughing (and yelling), R.E.P.O is absolutely worth playing.

Bought R.E.P.O. thinking it was a co-op horror game.
What I got instead was:
a piano that weighs approximately the same as the moon
a friend who dropped a priceless ceramic vase down the stairs immediately
a monster that only activates when someone says "is it safe"
and a cart we lost in the first two minutes and never spoke of again.
The objective is simple. Carry valuable items carefully to extraction. Do not break them. We have never once done this.
The physics system is a masterpiece of human suffering:
"Okay, careful, careful—"
The vase flies sideways into a wall.
It was worth $4,000.
We needed $4,000.
Dave is no longer allowed to touch things.
The proximity voice chat adds incredible immersion. You can hear your friends whispering in real time as you creep through a dark mansion. You can also hear the exact moment someone starts screaming because a monster that looks like a rejected Pixar villain walked through a door at 2% speed and somehow this is the most terrifying experience of our collective lives.
The monster AI is elegantly simple. It hears noise. We make noise. This is our entire relationship with death.
The upgrade shop offers meaningful progression. We bought better lungs. We needed better lungs because we keep screaming. We are still screaming. We just have more health while we do it.
10/10.
We never hit quota.
We're going back in.
Someone find the cart.

Probably the only "lethal company-like" (or whatever you wanna call it) that I like, including the original Lethal Company. While Lethal Company is still a good game and commendable for popularizing the gameplay loop it has, it's still primarily a game where you're meant to die in various ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ways for laughs. REPO still expects you to die eventually, but the tools you have are way stronger, and how you play the game can vary a lot on the gear you buy and the party you have. Early game REPO is more faithful to the original genre since you have very little gear, but once you get your first weapons the game really sets itself apart. You can absolutely play the game like a horror game and run away/hide from every enemy, but you can also play the game like it's DOOM and go around trying to kill every monster on the map. Weapons aside, there's a lot of very useful equipment that feels good to use. The point being is that the REPO devs do a great job of making the gameplay itself fun and engaging, instead of it essentially being a way to kill the player and make your friends laugh. Also, unlike plenty of other games in the genre this game gets consistent, and quality, updates. I can't think of a single update since launch that I thought was bad.

By far my favourite multiplayer game of all time. I adore the dev team and I hope they continue to produce that heartful and hilarious content they have been making at whatever pace is comfortable for them. It's such a fun game with so much replayability, and there's no game I'd have rather put five hundred hours of yelling, aurafarming and dying into than this one.  
 
It also helps me process grief, strangely enough, so that's cool.

R.E.P.O is easily one of the better co-op games on Steam. 
 
Far from “friend slop,” it’s got an addictive gameplay loop where every run feels different and never repetitive. The devs are extremely impressive with constant updates being released, frequent Q&As, and strong engagement with the community through suggestions and feedback. 
 
The physics mixed with proximity chat and the unique abilities and characteristics of each monster make it extremely entertaining and fun with mates. We planned on playing the base game and then moving on to modded, but with the frequency of the updates and the content, we have not found a need to try modded yet. 
 
If you want a game that delivers laughs, chaos, and chill sessions with friends, this is it. And for the price, you get an insane amount of value and playtime. Nominated 4 times for Steam Awards!

R.E.P.O. is an absolute hit.

This is a co-op PC Horror (but funny with friends) game that relies on physics, proximity voice chat, gradual ability upgrades, and weapons/traps of your choosing. The monsters can hear and/or see you. Different creatures have various levels of health as well as ways they may detect you. With other players you generally have better odds at surviving. The goal is to fill a cart with an assortment of valuable items till you reach a specified amount and bring to a designated location. As you progress it becomes more challenging from monsters, to the monetary goal.

An aspect I really appreciate is that even as you may die multiple times (with others still alive), you're not useless to the game. You can continue to chat with them for short periods- shouting helpful notes or sabotaging them by accident {usually).

The public lobbies can be fun if you don't have too many friends with this game, buttt... they should definitely get it by now!

I hope you enjoy it as much as I have! 11/10 game!

After around [b]70 hours[/b], R.E.P.O. became one of my favorite co-op games.

The game really shines in later quotas, where tension, panic, and teamwork come together. Moments where half the team is down and you're desperately searching for the last items to finish the quota are where the game is at its best.

It can also be really funny with the right people, sometimes you're trying to take it seriously and actually survive, and other times everything just turns into complete chaos. Both ways are fun in their own way.

Even after taking breaks for months or even a year, this is the type of game that still pulls you back. It's perfect for relaxed evenings with friends instead of competitive games that can get frustrating.

The game is still in [b]early access[/b], but the developers are actively improving it and adding new content based on feedback, which is great to see.

If you have friends to play with, [b]I'd highly recommend it.[/b]
